name: Jeremiyah Love
ceiling: Immediate every-down bell cow and top-5 dynasty RB; highest-drafted RB (No.3 overall) since Barkley, with elite receiving chops.
floor: Cardinals aren't handing him the job — OC Hackett won't name him starter and Tyler Allgeier opened camp with the 1st team; committee/goal-line usage early.
buzz: Unanimous RB1 of the class and consensus 1.01 in superflex. Slight July cooling as beat writers flag Hackett downplaying him, but the community is still all-in long-term.

name: Fernando Mendoza
ceiling: Franchise QB1 for a decade and a superflex cornerstone; No.1-pick pedigree (Heisman + title, fully guaranteed deal).
floor: Sits behind Kirk Cousins to open 2026; showed pro-style growing pains late in spring.
buzz: Signed July 23; Kubiak bringing him along slowly (3rd team in OTAs, 1st-team looks in camp). Strongly hyped — the only elite-tier passer in a weak QB class and the clear 1.01-1.03.

name: Carnell Tate
ceiling: Long-term WR1 and Cam Ward's clear No.1 target; unusually high floor for a rookie.
floor: Even the down case is a solid WR2/3 — little bust risk here.
buzz: HYPED. No.4 overall, running as de-facto WR1 with the 1st team; flashed in OTAs and built chemistry with Ward. OROY co-favorite and consensus class WR1 (KTC #2 rookie). Community strongly bullish.

name: Jordyn Tyson
ceiling: Highest ceiling in the class — alpha WR1 if healthy; elite separator taken No.8 overall.
floor: Injury-derailed bust risk — long college history (knee, collarbone, hamstrings).
buzz: OROY co-favorite but buyer-beware: Saints managing his hamstring history and Olave is limited. Pre-draft many had him class WR1; injury-wary analysts (FantasyLife) drop him to WR3.

name: Makai Lemon
ceiling: WR2 next to DeVonta Smith in a high-powered Eagles offense; 2025 Biletnikoff winner and unanimous All-American.
floor: Slot-capped complementary piece if the target tree stays crowded.
buzz: RISING. With A.J. Brown traded to New England, beat writers project Lemon as the No.2 receiver; says he is 100% for camp after a spring hamstring. Sentiment trending up (KTC #5 rookie).

name: Jadarian Price
ceiling: Standalone Seahawks RB1 — Macdonald has talked about using him extensively as more than a runner; Price says he is ready to be RB1.
floor: Late-1st NFL capital (No.32) with an unproven pass-pro/receiving projection; rotational if Seattle runs a committee.
buzz: Biggest post-draft riser of the class — the runaway RB2. July camp reports have him drawing a heavy workload. Community: buy now before the price climbs.

name: KC Concepcion
ceiling: Versatile YAC slot weapon who out-produces Jerry Jeudy; 1st-round capital gives him the inside track in the slot.
floor: Slot-only role in a bad-QB offense; loses reps in a training-camp battle with Isaiah Bond.
buzz: Murky sleeper. No.24 overall, but Cleveland's unsettled QB caps near-term value and the room is crowded (Jeudy, rookie Boston). Analysts split (KTC #7). Comps to Zay Flowers.

name: Ty Simpson
ceiling: McVay-developed heir to Stafford — the classic sit-a-year, break-out superflex stash.
floor: Small, inconsistent college sample; No.13 was called the most controversial pick of the first round.
buzz: Mildly fading. Up-and-down first camp; with Stafford resting, Simpson slid to backup behind Stetson Bennett in early reps, denting the draft-night hype.

name: Kenyon Sadiq
ceiling: Freak-athlete move TE (~4.39 / 43.5in vert) who becomes the Jets' matchup weapon and a low-end TE1.
floor: One-year college producer buried behind Mason Taylor; a multi-year TE3 who never earns targets.
buzz: FADING / bust-risk chatter. Missed OTAs + minicamp after late-May hernia surgery; Bleacher Report tagged him the Jets' biggest bust. Still the class TE1 on most boards (FantasyPros No.8) but sentiment cooling vs. Stowers.

name: Omar Cooper Jr.
ceiling: Steady WR2/flex in three-WR sets; No.30 overall (Jets traded up).
floor: Fourth mouth to feed behind Wilson, Mitchell and Mason Taylor; minimal early target share.
buzz: SLEEPER. Beat writer Rich Cimini called him the Jets' most impressive spring rookie, all but locking the No.3 WR job. Quietly liked by the community (KTC #9).

name: Denzel Boston
ceiling: Red-zone-winning big-body X (6-4, 20 college TDs, 14 in the red zone).
floor: Depth/rotational — needs to be special to matter, buried behind Jeudy/Concepcion in a bad-QB offense.
buzz: MUTED. No.39 overall, Browns' second rookie WR; both projected as contributors but he sits third in the pecking order. Analysts lukewarm (KTC #11) — a late-value dart.

name: Eli Stowers
ceiling: Goedert's heir in 2027 as a slot-mismatch weapon for Jalen Hurts; led all FBS TEs in receiving yards per game in 2025.
floor: Year-1 backup behind Goedert with limited snaps until his blocking improves.
buzz: SLEEPER / long-game value. QB-turned-TE with an elite combine (45.5in vert); Sirianni wants him in the slot. Analysts call him the safer long-term bet than Sadiq on production, with Goedert on an expiring deal.

name: Nicholas Singleton
ceiling: Post-Pollard lead back in Tennessee — former five-star with league-winning stash upside if he inherits the backfield.
floor: Fell to Round 5; buried behind Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears after an underwhelming final college year.
buzz: One of the more interesting cheap stashes — could be Pollard's backup by Week 1. Big split: upside bettors have him Round 2, DynastyNerds much lower (RB40s).

name: Jonah Coleman
ceiling: Short-yardage/goal-line hammer who develops into a dual threat and passes injury-prone J.K. Dobbins.
floor: Bad landing spot — 4th-round (108th), opens as the No.3 back behind Dobbins and RJ Harvey.
buzz: Going RB3/RB4, early-2nd in superflex. Talented bowling-ball back but capital + depth chart cap the role. Sleeper if Dobbins misses time; buzz is profile-based, no standout camp rep yet.

name: Antonio Williams
ceiling: Immediate WR2 opposite McLaurin in a target-vacated offense; a genuine OROY dark-horse with Jayden Daniels throwing.
floor: Reliable PPR slot floor even in the down case.
buzz: HYPED. Reported to camp with the No.2 job wide open after Deebo's departure; praised by Dan Quinn for pro-ready routes and tagged an underrated rookie by ESPN. Best-value Day-2 WR per the community.

name: Germie Bernard
ceiling: Eventual WR2 if Metcalf/Pittman age out; among the savviest route-runners in the class.
floor: Buried as WR3/4 behind DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman with modest rookie targets amid QB uncertainty.
buzz: Rising camp stock but capped opportunity — beat writers expect him to pass Roman Wilson for WR3 quickly. Analysts call him a better real-life fit than fantasy target (DLF high-end WR4).

name: Emmett Johnson
ceiling: Passing-down role in the Chiefs offense right away, with league-winning upside if Kenneth Walker misses time.
floor: 5th-round capital; a handcuff to Walker with Demercado competing for third-down snaps.
buzz: Freshest positive camp story of the mid-round group — already RB2 on the depth chart, first on the practice field, standout pass-catcher. Sentiment clearly rising.

name: Zachariah Branch
ceiling: Explosive slot/gadget WR2 + return man who becomes a Waddle-style YAC weapon in the Falcons offense.
floor: Fourth-option, low-volume rotational slot/returner with a fantasy-irrelevant target share.
buzz: HYPED in late-July camp as the WR with the highest ceiling for the open slot job. But split-to-cautious analysts moved him down post-draft (~WR13 rookie), citing his 177-lb frame and screen-heavy college usage.

name: Chris Bell
ceiling: Eventual physical X (6-2, 220, 4.4) — first-round talent that fell on injury.
floor: Lost rookie year / never fully recovers from the ACL.
buzz: STASH. On the active/NFI list to open camp (cannot practice; return months away). Some call him massively underrated buy-low, but 2026 expectations are near-zero — a patience play (KTC #15 rookie).

name: De'Zhaun Stribling
ceiling: WR2/3 in a Purdy-Shanahan offense if he wins a perimeter role; 6-2 with 4.36 speed and reliable hands.
floor: Buried behind Evans, Kirk and Pearsall; older prospect with a thin target-earning profile.
buzz: HYPED in camp — flashing speed, moved up with Kirk's calf strain, praised by Purdy as reliable. ADP climbing fast; FantasyPros cautions age/production risk (19th, Tier 4). Borderline overvalued vs. profile.

name: Elijah Sarratt
ceiling: NFL-ready possession/contested-catch WR who wins the slot-Z role in a Lamar Jackson offense.
floor: Depth/red-zone contributor stuck behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman.
buzz: Genuine sleeper hype — flashed all spring and is forcing into the starter conversation, reportedly outplaying fellow rookie Ja'Kobi Lane. Valued for reliability over athleticism (FantasyPros WR12).

name: Carson Beck
ceiling: Prototype build + arm with 43 college starts; could start for Arizona in 2026 and gain quick fantasy relevance.
floor: Limited runway and a trade candidate if he starts; overconfidence flags from scouts.
buzz: Rising sleeper — CBS has him climbing the SF top-50 and one AFC scout says he is more talented than Simpson. Dynasty rankers still slot him below Simpson on R3 vs R1 capital.

name: Mike Washington Jr.
ceiling: Elite athlete (perfect RAS, 4.33, 39in vert at 223) who wins the Raiders RB2 job in Kubiak's multi-RB scheme.
floor: Competing with Laube/Collier; trade value already down to a late-2027 3rd, reflecting a murky role.
buzz: Analyst-labeled buy-low sleeper on athletic profile + scheme fit. No specific July rep report — buzz is profile/scheme-based.

name: Kaytron Allen
ceiling: Penn State's all-time leading rusher who wins a wide-open Commanders competition as the early-down back.
floor: 6th-round (187th), skipped athletic testing, buried behind Croskey-Merritt, White and Ford — realistic best case RB3.
buzz: Lukewarm post-draft (DLF 7/18). Community sees a productive-college/poor-capital profile — mild deep-stash interest, mostly wait-and-see.

name: Malachi Fields
ceiling: Big-bodied (6-4) boundary X who grows into a quality starter alongside Jaxson Dart, especially if Slayton departs.
floor: Rotational outside backup buried behind Nabers, Slayton and Mooney; ~158 projected rookie yards.
buzz: Stood out at rookie minicamp (contested catches, slants). Analysts call him alluring — a stash-with-upside on size + Dart's vertical style — tempered by a crowded room and a 4.61 forty.

name: Chris Brazzell II
ceiling: Field-stretching deep threat — 6-4, 4.37, absurd catch radius; projects as a Week 1 outside starter opposite Tetairoa McMillan.
floor: Boom-or-bust WR4 — Bryce Young caps volume, lets corners into his body, and he is in a WR2 competition.
buzz: SLEEPER — nearly made the play of camp with a leaping deep grab from Young, but cooling on late-July knee soreness that gave Legette reps. Analysts like the spot, temper it as boom/bust.

name: Cade Klubnik
ceiling: League-average starter if everything aligns; behind a Geno Smith bridge, so a runway exists.
floor: Inconsistent decision-making and R4 capital; competing just for the QB2 job.
buzz: Notable community riser — Jets fans flipped on him after rookie minicamp and he impressed the QB coach. The most-hyped of the Day-3 QBs.

name: Oscar Delp
ceiling: Athletic seam-busting three-down starter and 2027 Saints TE1; 4.49 forty, 96th-pct explosion.
floor: Buried developmental TE2/3 behind Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant; a taxi-squad flier.
buzz: SLEEPER / patient stash — an athletic freak who played 2025 on a foot fracture. Appeal is 2027+; no standout July camp report, buzz is profile/opportunity-based.
